label: paragraph_title
text: New Conflict, or Present Situation?

label: text
text: "Le Temps," in an editorial, dwells on the difficulties of con-ړed action in China.

label: text
text: 1. “Says a — “Firstly, within China itself there exists the sentiment of political independence.

label: text
text: "Society, apart from internal resistance" which such a policy might provoke in a country "where the Government is without authority, it may be asked whether an agreement could easily be realised between the Powers directly interested" in the Far East. "Voices have already been raised in the United States protesting against a joint policy, the effect of which might be to throw China into the arms of Soviet Russia."

label: text
text: “Le Temps” urges that no hasty decision be reached lest a conflict might be let loose which would be graver than the present situation.— $ ^{9} $Reuter.

label: text
text: The Daily Express at Paris understands from the French Foreign Office that France will remain neutral in the event of a dispute with China.

label: text
text: In view of the foregoing, the following cableg published yesterday are of particular interest:—

label: text
text: “Les Temps” points out that this is not the first time that a common policy of the Powers (in China) has been contemplated; but hitherto difficulties were always encountered; preventing effective action in this direction.

label: text
text: That Japan is not making a decisive move at present is indicated in the following:—

label: text
text: This morning the Cabinet discussed the Chinese situation, but beyond agreeing to the necessity for maintaining a very vigilant watch on possible developments. label: paragraph_title
text: NEXT CHINA WAR.

label: text
text: CANTON'S AMBITIONS.

label: text
text: Only the next few months can tell whether Marshal Sun Chuan-fang was wise in delaying material aid for his professed superior, Wu Pei-fu.

label: text
text: Gossips say that Sun Chuanfang purposely deferred entry into the Act, that if Wu Pei-fu wasгоff and he could act for his own benefit. If, on the other hand, Nationalists were vanquished, he could not have been drawn into the Act. It has to be admitted that if he disposes of the Canton Party, his power will be greater than that of Wu Pei-fu at his zenith.

label: text
text: But the question now is whether Sun Chulan-fang, on his own resources, can crush Chang Kai-shek. That a new war will be in progress there seems little doubt as the southerners are now branching out.

label: text
text: Although Marshal Sun nominally rules five provinces it cannot be taken for granted that all the generals and people therein will rally to his standard, especially at a time when Chang Kai-shek has proved a formidable foe.

label: text
text: Should Chang Kai-shek respect Sun Chuan-fang's declaration of neutrality, the only concern then will be one of balance of power.

label: text
text: Then there is Marshal Chang Tso-lin and his Fengtien Party to consider. Eighteen months ago, he suffered a check by Sun Chuanfang. The Manchu partisans had extended an arm to Shanghai, to the rich area around. When Sun Chuan-fang struck, they hastily withdrew northwards.

label: text
text: Perhaps Chang Tso-lin will be satisfied to rule the North.

label: text
text: Admiral Tu Hsi-kwel, who was nominated by Wu Pei-fu for the acting Premiership in the absence of a President, is now without support and the Fengtienites are putting forward the name of Chien Yun-peng as the new Premier.

label: text
text: In Canton's Favour?

label: text
text: One considered opinion is that Fengtien will be contented to leave the territory south of the Yellow River to Sun Chuan-fang.

label: text
text: The consensus of opinion is that Sun Chuan-fang has moved too late; and that Chang Tso-lin will mark time until necessary—when he will fight the final with the survivor. Their old animosity is a factor in favour of the Nationalists.

label: text
text: A great deal hinges on what are Canton's ambitions so far. They are not pursuing Wu Pei-fu (who still has a large army in "Honan province") but appear to be diverting their attention to consolidating the "South first.

text: WAR PUZZLES.

label: text
text: LULL SETS IN ON THE FRONT.

label: text
text: WU PEI-FU'S BOAST.

label: text
text: News from the front in China's war indicates that a lull has set in.

label: text
text: A puzzle is set for those not in know. After a feverish onslaught the southerners now appear to be resting instead of pursuing Wu Pei-fu's army.

label: text
text: Most battling of all is the persistence of a claim that Wuchang is still held by the northerners while the fall of Hankow and Hanyang is admitted. Heights near Hanyang (arsenal) would ensile? pave the way towards the capture of Wuchang, the capital of Hupeb province.

label: text
text: Wu Pei-fu is still issuing communiques. He talks of sending de-tachments southwards to turn the flanks of the southern vanguard. But reading between the lines, it seems that he is, at the most, trying to rally his men some distance to the north of Hankow.

label: text
text:

by the northerners.

label: text
text: Another inexplicable factor is the attitude of the adherents of Wu Pei-fu. There are several near Peking, such as Chi "Hsieh-yuan", who are fighters of renown with armies of 20,000 to 30,000 but they have not been thrown into the battle. A Chinese military expert in Hongkong has informed the "China Mail" that this was anticipated. Instead of tiring fresh troops, Wu Pei-fu will make a stand on his second line of defence.

text: Marshall Chang Tso-lin gives the impression of being more concerned with consolidating his hold on Peking, than offering help to Wu Pei-fu. Should the southerners cross the Yellow River, then the Fengtian Party will take the field, it is anticipated.

text: Generally, hostilities have quietened down and the danger of new wars breaking out is not so apparent.

text: Chow Yam-yan, Tupan of Fukien, has done nothing further towards his threatened invasion of Kwangtung.

label: text
text: AN EX-ATTORNEY GENERAL ON TRIAL.

label: text
text: CHAMPAGNE DINNER STORY

label: text
text: New York, Sept. 10

label: text
text: At his trial Henry Daugherty, ex-Attorney-General, said he suggested giving King, the intermediary, something for aiding in securing the reimbursement for the sale of the Metals Company. Later, at King's request, he gave him a cheque for $50,000 at a champagne dinner in New York attended by Miller, King and Smith. The last-named (who is now deceased) was an associate of Daugherty and Miller, and he then handed Herr Merton cheques for $7,000,000. Herr Merton on the same occasion ordered $391,000 worth of Liberty Bonds to be delivered to a local bond broker.

label: text
text: The Government contends that the $50,000 cheque and these Bonds constitute a bribe shared by Daugherty and Miller for approving of the return of the $7,000,000 to Herr Merton.—Reuter's American Service.
